title: Granth and Panth
hookLine: scripture and community together carry the Guru

cards: Stand at the back of a gurdwara hall and look forward. At the front, on a raised platform under a canopy, the Guru Granth Sahib, wrapped in cloth, someone sitting behind it waving a whisk. Now look down.

Between you and the Granth, rows of people sitting on the floor: grandmothers, teenagers, a man still in his work uniform, a toddler wandering between laps. A book and a crowd. Yesterday, the Guru was the Word.
Today, the Word doesn't travel alone.

teach.h: GRANTH: THE BOOK. PANTH: THE PEOPLE.
teach.b: Granth means the book, the scripture: yesterday's Word, given a body of pages. Panth means the path, and by extension the people who walk it together, the Sikh community.
Sikh tradition remembers that Guru Gobind Singh named no human successor. Instead, tradition says, he passed the guruship to the Granth and to the Panth, the Khalsa community.
Sikhs sum it up in a short phrase: Guru Granth, Guru Panth. The Guru as book. The Guru as people.
What makes a crowd a congregation? Guru Nanak asks it in Sri Raag. In paraphrase: how is the true congregation known?
And he answers: it is where the One Name is spoken. So the sangat isn't holy because of who's in it, or how important they are. It's holy because of what's spoken there.
Why do the two need each other? A book on a shelf with nobody reading it is silent. A crowd with nothing at the center can drift anywhere, toward whoever is loudest.
Together, each keeps the other honest. The people read and sing the Granth, so the Word has a voice. The Granth holds the people to something older and steadier than any one of them.
Tradition says that when Sikhs gather to decide serious matters, they do it in the Guru's presence, with the Granth in the room.

how: Sikhs gather as sangat in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib, and speak of the Guru as present in both the scripture and the Khalsa Panth, in the phrase Guru Granth, Guru Panth.

games.q: you're Guru Gobind Singh, and the question is who leads after you. tradition says you choose what?
o: a son or a chosen disciple as the next human Guru.
the scripture and the community together.
a council of scholars with the final word.
games.why: Sikh tradition remembers that Guru Gobind Singh named no human successor and passed the guruship to the Granth and the Panth.

practice: Bring to mind the people who have sat beside you in something good, a family table, a service, a hospital room, a circle of friends, and see them one by one until the room fills up.
Then breathe as if you were all breathing together, and if you pray, let Waheguru be the word spoken in that room.

wordCard.voice: Granth and Panth. The scripture and the community, which together, Sikh tradition says, carry the Guru. Today's word.
